raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

#37577 (Aaronson-Gumbel text watermarking) added `redact_watermark_secrets` to the request-log formatters. Both `_dataclass_to_string_truncated` and `_transform_data_for_logging` redact the whole request object **before** truncation and **before** `skip_names` filtering, so every `--log-requests` call walks the full `input_ids` element by element (~0.5us/token). With long prompts this costs tens of ms per log call on the tokenizer-manager event loop, on receive and again on finish, and shows up directly in TTFT.

On main, formatting an 80k-token `GenerateReqInput` at `--log-requests-level 2` costs ~62 ms (text) / ~60 ms (json); with this PR it is ~0.3 ms / ~1.1 ms.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/srt/utils/request_logger.py`:

- New `_redact_field`: redact by field/key name. Fields named `watermark_key` / `watermark_key_b` / `watermark_config` become `<redacted>`; `watermark` / `sampling_params` / `preferred_sampling_params` are redacted recursively; everything else passes through untouched. `skip_names` fields are dropped before redaction.
- The `str(...)` fallback in both formatters still redacts first, so a msgspec Struct carrying watermark fields under an ordinary key stays redacted, exactly as on main.
- The truncated-list branch of `_transform_data_for_logging` now transforms each printed item instead of returning raw items, so a truncated list of dataclasses/Structs no longer breaks `json.dumps`.

`python/sglang/srt/sampling/watermarking/core.py`:

- The watermark field-name sets are now module-level `WATERMARK_SECRET_FIELD_NAMES` / `WATERMARK_CONTAINER_FIELD_NAMES`, shared by all redact branches and the logger instead of being re-listed in five places.
- New scalar fast-path: `_SCALAR_TYPES.issuperset(map(type, value))` scans a sequence in C, and a plain-scalar sequence (e.g. token ids) can never hold a secret, since secrets only sit under dict keys or struct/dataclass fields. Mutable lists come back as copies (the crash-dump path pickles the result on a worker thread); immutable tuples may alias. The mixed-container walk skips scalar items inline. This bounds the other `redact_watermark_secrets` callers too — `dump_requests` / crash dump in `tokenizer_manager.py`, server info — and list-of-lists batched `input_ids`.

Log output is byte-identical to main at every `--log-requests-level`, with one intentional exception: Struct/dataclass items inside truncated json lists now print as redacted strings instead of crashing `json.dumps`.

## Accuracy Tests

Logging-only change; no model path touched.

New `test/registered/unit/utils/test_request_logger_redaction.py` (CPU, `base-a-test-cpu`):

- Secrets are redacted in both formatters, for 16 and 100k input ids, including the top-level `GenerateReqInput.watermark` field.
- A msgspec Struct with a `watermark_key` field under an ordinary key stays redacted (regression test for the string fallback).
- Truncated lists keep their printed halves redacted; a truncated json list of Structs stays `json.dumps`-serializable.
- The redaction walk is bounded at each level's real `(max_length, skip_names)` — this test fails on main.
- Scalar sequences skip the walk; mutable lists come back as copies while tuples may alias; containers are still redacted.

Output equivalence vs main was checked with both formatters over 22 payload shapes (levels 0-3 metadata, nested secrets, msgspec Structs under ordinary fields, long secret-bearing lists, batched `input_ids`, finish `out` dicts, tuples, None secrets, unicode text): byte-identical in all 44 runs, no secret string in any output.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

CPU, single thread:

| case | main (ms) | PR (ms) |
|---|---:|---:|
| level 2, text, 80k input_ids | 61.6 | 0.3 |
| level 2, json, 80k input_ids | 59.6 | 1.1 |
| scalar list redact, 100k ids | 74.4 | 2.3 |
| mixed 100k scalars + 1 dict | 74.2 | 5.8 |
| batched 32x4k `input_ids`, level 2 text | 204.6 | 14.0 |
| level 3, text, 80k input_ids (prints every id) | 127.0 | 9.2 |
| crash-dump-shaped redact (80k prompt + 20k `output_ids`) | 14.7 | 0.5 |

Level 3 and batched requests remain dominated by `str()` of the ids they print; the redaction on top is now a C-level scan.

Related: #44683 (closed) fixed the same logger path with a different split (it skipped the walk only for `skip_names` fields and long non-watermark lists). This PR redacts strictly by field name and additionally bounds the other `redact_watermark_secrets` callers via the core fast-path.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). N/A, no user-facing change.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

+"""Watermark secrets stay redacted in request logs, and the redaction walk is
+bounded by max_length instead of the prompt length."""
+
+import json
+import unittest
+from unittest import mock
+
+import msgspec
+
+from sglang.srt.managers.io_struct import GenerateReqInput
+from sglang.srt.sampling.watermarking.core import redact_watermark_secrets
+from sglang.srt.utils import request_logger
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=1, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+SECRET = "super-secret-watermark-key"
+
+
+class ExtraOptions(msgspec.Struct):
+    watermark_key: str = SECRET
+    note: str = "x"
+
+
+def _request(num_ids: int) -> GenerateReqInput:
+    return GenerateReqInput(
+        input_ids=list(range(num_ids)),
+        sampling_params={"max_new_tokens": 8, "watermark": {"key": SECRET}},
+        rid="rid-0",
+    )
+
+
+class _LongestWalkSpy:
+    """Records the longest list redact_watermark_secrets is asked to walk."""
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        self.real = request_logger.redact_watermark_secrets
+        self.longest = 0
+
+    def __call__(self, value, **kwargs):
+        self._scan(value)
+        return self.real(value, **kwargs)
+
+    def _scan(self, value):
+        if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):
+            self.longest = max(self.longest, len(value))
+            for item in value:
+                self._scan(item)
+        elif isinstance(value, dict):
+            for item in value.values():
+                self._scan(item)
+
+
+class TestRequestLogRedaction(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_secrets_redacted_in_both_formatters(self):
+        for num_ids in (16, 100_000):
+            req = _request(num_ids)
+            text_out = request_logger._dataclass_to_string_truncated(req)
+            json_out = repr(request_logger._transform_data_for_logging(req))
+            self.assertNotIn(SECRET, text_out)
+            self.assertNotIn(SECRET, json_out)
+            self.assertIn("<redacted>", text_out)
+
+    def test_top_level_watermark_field_is_redacted(self):
+        req = GenerateReqInput(
+            input_ids=[1, 2, 3],
+            watermark={"enabled": True, "key": SECRET},
+            rid="rid-0",
+        )
+        text_out = request_logger._dataclass_to_string_truncated(req)
+        json_out = repr(request_logger._transform_data_for_logging(req))
+        self.assertNotIn(SECRET, text_out)
+        self.assertNotIn(SECRET, json_out)
+
+    def test_struct_under_ordinary_field_is_redacted(self):
+        payload = {"rid": "r1", "extra": ExtraOptions()}
+        text_out = request_logger._dataclass_to_string_truncated(payload)
+        json_out = repr(request_logger._transform_data_for_logging(payload))
+        self.assertNotIn(SECRET, text_out)
+        self.assertNotIn(SECRET, json_out)
+        self.assertIn("<redacted>", text_out)
+
+    def test_truncated_list_halves_stay_redacted(self):
+        payload = {"items": [{"watermark_key": SECRET}] * 5000}
+        text_out = request_logger._dataclass_to_string_truncated(payload)
+        json_out = repr(request_logger._transform_data_for_logging(payload))
+        self.assertNotIn(SECRET, text_out)
+        self.assertNotIn(SECRET, json_out)
+        self.assertIn("<redacted>", text_out)
+
+    def test_truncated_json_list_of_structs_is_serializable(self):
+        payload = {"items": [ExtraOptions()] * 5000}
+        transformed = request_logger._transform_data_for_logging(payload)
+        dumped = json.dumps(transformed)
+        self.assertNotIn(SECRET, dumped)
+
+    def test_redaction_walk_is_bounded_by_max_length(self):
+        for level in (0, 1, 2, 3):
+            max_length, skip_names, _ = request_logger.RequestLogger(
+                log_requests=True,
+                log_requests_level=level,
+                log_requests_format="text",
+                log_requests_target=None,
+            ).metadata
+            if level == 3:
+                # Level 3 prints every input id, so the walk is inherently unbounded.
+                continue
+            bound = min(max_length, 2048)
+            for fn in (
+                request_logger._dataclass_to_string_truncated,
+                request_logger._transform_data_for_logging,
+            ):
+                spy = _LongestWalkSpy()
+                with mock.patch.object(request_logger, "redact_watermark_secrets", spy):
+                    fn(_request(100_000), max_length, skip_names)
+                self.assertLessEqual(spy.longest, bound, f"level={level} {fn.__name__}")
+
+    def test_scalar_sequences_skip_the_redaction_walk(self):
+        ids = list(range(100_000))
+        redacted = redact_watermark_secrets(ids)
+        self.assertEqual(redacted, ids)
+        # The dump path ships the result to a worker thread, so the mutable
+        # list must come back as a copy; tuples are immutable and may alias.
+        self.assertIsNot(redacted, ids)
+        ids_tuple = tuple(ids)
+        self.assertIs(redact_watermark_secrets(ids_tuple), ids_tuple)
+        redacted = redact_watermark_secrets([{"watermark_key": SECRET}])
+        self.assertEqual(redacted, [{"watermark_key": "<redacted>"}])
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
